note: Lighthouse 12.x, identical flags for both sides in one sitting (throttlingMethod=simulate, headless Chrome new, categories performance/accessibility/best-practices/seo). Both sides served as plain static files over http://127.0.0.1 so the Firebase SDK never loads. The baseline side is `git archive 332258f` (F2); the F3 side is the working tree at commit bfd6cc0 plus the F3.6 changes. Two full A/B runs were executed back to back; the numbers below are the second run, and the first run differed by at most 3 ms on LCP.

whyThePerfDelta.detail: wishlist.html +33729 bytes (the F3 markup and the inline render code) and the css total +16692 bytes (css/dashboard-v16.css alone 9393 -> 32573 bytes). Total +50231 bytes, matching the +49 KB transfer. The transfer is uncompressed: the harness serves raw files over a local static server with no gzip. This app is one render-blocking HTML file plus CSS, and FCP == LCP in every run, so extra render-blocking bytes move LCP almost 1:1 under simulated throttling.
whyThePerfDelta.notTheCause: No new origin, no new font, no new image, no new third-party script, no blocking work: TBT is 0 ms on both sides in both form factors, and CLS is 0.
whyThePerfDelta.unchanged: Accessibility went 96 -> 100 on both form factors (the two contrast fixes below).

accessibilityFindingsFixedInF3.before: 4.39:1 (15px/400 dark text on #7565e8) - the pre-existing P2-2 that F1 and F2 both reported
2.09:1 worst case (measured across every gradient stop composited with the .28 white glow)

noFpsClaims: No frame-rate figure is claimed anywhere in this report. The motion work is described by what is measurable: which properties animate (opacity/transform only), that reduced-motion removes it, and that TBT stays 0 ms and CLS stays 0.
